assumptions.basis: Reported growth was approximately 2% in prior-year Q4, 3% in FY2026 Q1 and 1% in Q2, with Q2 organic growth flat. Base assumes modest growth between the seasonal reference and latest reading; bear assumes contraction and bull a recovery above recent growth. These are total reported-growth assumptions, without separately adding historical FX, price or mix contributions.

Prior-year Q4 gross margin was approximately 49.11%, versus 51.37% and 51.22% in recent Q1 and Q2. Base allows partial retention of recent margins while respecting the lower Q4 seasonal reference. Bear assumes deterioration below prior-year Q4; bull assumes recent margin strength persists. Cost and mix mechanisms are illustrative judgments without supplied market evidence.

Prior-year Q4 SG&A/sales was approximately 28.26%, versus 25.21% in recent Q1 and 27.05% in Q2. Base stays close to the seasonal Q4 reference rather than extrapolating Q1's low ratio. Bear assumes expense pressure and weaker sales absorption; bull assumes improved expense efficiency. Higher ratios are adverse.

Contract-defined historical component totals were 166 in prior-year Q4, 179 in recent Q1 and 55 in Q2. Base rounds to a cautious positive contribution between the latest and seasonal references; bear allows a net expense and bull a stronger positive contribution. No interest-rate, debt-balance or exceptional-gain forecast is asserted.

Reported rates were 19.8% in prior-year Q4, 20.8% in recent Q1 and 20.1% in Q2. Base rounds near the seasonal and latest references; bear assumes a higher tax burden and bull a lower burden, near the supplied FY2025 Q3 rate of 18.6%. No specific tax benefit or jurisdictional mix change is forecast.

Total less attributable net income gives 11 in prior-year Q4, 31 in recent Q1 and 12 in Q2. Base follows the latest reading and seasonal reference. Bear assumes a larger deduction from total earnings, near Q1; bull assumes a modestly smaller deduction. Ownership and subsidiary earnings details are unavailable.

Attributable earnings divided by rounded diluted EPS imply approximately 2442.6 million shares in prior-year Q4 and 2426.4 million in latest Q2. Base assumes only a modest further decline; bear allows the denominator to remain near the prior-year level and bull assumes a larger decline. Lower shares favor EPS; none of these values establishes an observed or authorized repurchase program.

Quarterly OCF/total net income was approximately 1.375 in prior-year Q4 and 1.148 in latest Q2. Base gives greater weight to the same-quarter seasonal reference but discounts its repeatability. Bear assumes weaker cash conversion; bull assumes stronger conversion above prior-year Q4. Working-capital timing is uncertain and these ratios are not annualized.

Positive capex outflow/sales was approximately 4.77% in prior-year Q4 and 5.25% in latest Q2. Base lies between these references. Bear assumes greater spending intensity and bull lower near-term cash outflow. Capital-spending timing is seasonal; no project pipeline or deferred-investment claim is supported.

findings.subject: Dates and seasonal baseline
findings.finding: All supplied publication dates precede the 2026-03-31 availability cutoff. FY2025 Q4 quarterly sales of USD 20,889 million correctly anchor target FY2026 Q4 sales; annual sales are not substituted. Missing FY2026 Q3 and target outcomes are disclosed.

findings.subject: Finance arithmetic, units and double counting
findings.finding: Mapped ratios and component totals agree with original packet amounts to stated rounding. Percent-to-decimal conversion, positive capex outflow, total-income cash conversion and attributable-income EPS treatment follow the contract. Historical growth contributions are not added again to scenario growth; other income is included once below modeled operating income.

findings.subject: Unresolved source inconsistencies
findings.finding: Original excerpts support the disclosed USD 1 million FY2025 Q3 reconciliation differences and FY2026 Q1 component total of 179 versus pretax-minus-operating of 178. Other-income labels vary. Contract placement is transparent, but neither the discrepancies nor external source classifications are resolved.

findings.subject: Scenario bounds and interpretation
findings.finding: All nine scenario rows respect contractual units and ranges. Adverse/favorable directions are coherent for the applicable earnings or cash-flow measure. Base values reference eligible seasonal and recent history; spreads are explicitly analyst judgments. Lower capex is appropriately limited to near-term cash flow, and share counts are not presented as observed repurchases.

findings.subject: Research causality and unsupported precision
findings.finding: Empty evidence appropriately produces no research signals or claimed market sensitivities. Rounded ratios and inferred shares are disclosed as approximations; scenario values are assumptions rather than precise observations. No insurance-specific claims or invented cash/debt facts appear.

findings.subject: Quotation fidelity
findings.finding: Several finance fields labeled source_excerpt concatenate or truncate original rows. Their numerical content is supported by the original packet, but those assembled strings are not single verbatim excerpts.

assumptions.basis: Preserve the frozen base and bull: prior-year Q4 reported growth was approximately 2%, recent Q1 3% and Q2 1%, with Q2 organic growth flat. Lower the control bear of -2% by one combined 0.5 percentage-point demand sensitivity for PG02 affordability pressure and PG04 weak spending. This is an illustrative reported-sales effect, not measured company volume elasticity; the two signals are not added separately. PG01 annual organic guidance provides context only, without imposing its range on quarterly reported growth or adding historical FX again.

Preserve the control base and bull, anchored by approximately 49.11% prior-year Q4 margin and 51.37%/51.22% recent Q1/Q2 margins. Lower the control bear of 48% by a single combined 50 basis-point residual cost sensitivity reflecting PG01 tariff uncertainty and PG03 upstream inflation. PPI stress is contained within this budget, not stacked separately. Commodity neutrality and annual FX guidance temper the interpretation and support no base change. This additional adverse stress is a judgment about possible deterioration beyond historical margins, not an allocation of annual after-tax guidance; procurement timing is unknown.

Unchanged from control: approximately 28.26% prior-year Q4, 25.21% recent Q1 and 27.05% Q2 support a seasonal base near 28%. Bear assumes weaker expense absorption; bull assumes improved efficiency. Higher ratios reduce profitability. No specific eligible evidence supports an incremental SG&A adjustment.

Unchanged from control: contract component totals of 166 in prior-year Q4, 179 in Q1 and 55 in Q2 support a cautious positive base. Bear allows net expense; bull stronger income. PG05's maintained policy range does not establish company repricing exposure, so no monetary rate adjustment is added. Its unsupported claim about PG01 interest/tax guidance is excluded.

Unchanged from control: reported rates of 19.8% in prior-year Q4, 20.8% in Q1 and 20.1% in Q2 support a 20% base. Bear increases the tax burden; bull is near the historical 18.6% Q3 rate. No supplied evidence establishes a specific incremental tax benefit, charge or jurisdictional change.

Unchanged from control: total less attributable income was 11 in prior-year Q4, 31 in Q1 and 12 in Q2. Base follows latest and seasonal references. A larger deduction is adverse to attributable earnings; a smaller deduction is favorable. Subsidiary and ownership details do not support further adjustment.

Unchanged from control: attributable income divided by rounded EPS implies approximately 2442.6 million prior-year Q4 shares and 2426.4 million latest Q2 shares. Base assumes modest further decline, bear a denominator near the prior-year level and bull a larger decline. Lower shares favor EPS, rather than operating profit. These are approximate scenario denominators, not evidence of an authorized repurchase program.

Unchanged from control: quarterly OCF/total net income was approximately 1.375 in prior-year Q4 and 1.148 in latest Q2. Base emphasizes Q4 seasonality while discounting repeatability; bear and bull represent weaker and stronger cash conversion. Market evidence does not quantify incremental working-capital effects. Higher conversion favors cash generation; ratios are not annualized.

Unchanged from control: positive capex outflow/sales was approximately 4.77% in prior-year Q4 and 5.25% in latest Q2. Base lies between these references. Bear assumes greater spending intensity and bull lower near-term cash outflow; this orientation concerns free cash flow, not immediate earnings or long-term investment quality. No project pipeline supports an incremental change.

findings.subject: Initial reconciliation blockers resolved within displayed precision
findings.finding: Supplemental original excerpts for FY2025 Q3 and FY2026 Q1 explicitly state that rows and columns may not add due to rounding. Independently recomputed Q3 residuals are +1, -1 and +1 USD million; Q1 component income of 179 differs from the displayed pretax-minus-operating bridge of 178 by 1 USD million. These residuals are compatible with rounding the participating amounts to whole millions. This resolves the initial blocker for a narrowly scoped illustrative model without changing reported values or asserting an exact reconciliation. The curator's USD 2 million tolerance is not a company-issued rule and is unnecessary to this conclusion.

findings.subject: Transcription-dependent market support
findings.finding: PG01's quotation supports commodity neutrality; its 0–4% organic guidance and annual after-tax tariff/FX amounts depend on factual transcriptions. PG02–PG04 numerical quotation fragments agree with the extracted facts, but complete labels, periods and adjustment bases are partly transcription-dependent. PG05 quotes the rate range, while the maintained decision and date depend on transcription. No supplied quotation contradicts these records, but independent source accuracy remains unverified.

findings.subject: Other-income classification
findings.finding: Original labels say operating in Q3 and FY2026 Q1/Q2, versus non-operating in FY2025 Q4. The outputs preserve this ambiguity and use the explicit contract aggregate as a model bridge. Q2's 55 USD million bridge reconciles exactly. This supports model aggregation, not certification of the accounting classification.

findings.subject: Dates, units and finance mapping
findings.finding: Supplied publication dates precede the cutoff. FY2025 Q4 quarterly sales of 20,889 USD million correctly anchor April–June 2026, excluding annual columns. Reviewed ratios, signed interest aggregation, noncontrolling deductions, positive capex outflows and percentage conversions agree with supplied history. Share denominators are appropriately disclosed as approximations from rounded EPS.

findings.subject: Scenario ranges, causal interpretation and double counting
findings.finding: All nine drivers remain within contractual bounds. Every base and all unrelated scenarios match the frozen control. Only bear sales growth decreases by 0.005 and bear gross margin by 0.005. Overlapping household signals share one demand sensitivity; tariff/PPI signals share one cost sensitivity. Magnitudes are explicitly uncalibrated analyst judgments. Annual organic guidance is not imposed on quarterly reported growth, and annual after-tax costs are not mechanically allocated to quarterly pretax margins.

findings.subject: Unsupported interest/tax overlap statement
findings.finding: PG05's packet overlap note claims PG01 contains annual interest/tax headwinds, which neither PG01 evidence surface supports. Reviewed outputs explicitly exclude that claim, so it supplies no modeled adjustment. Policy rates also remain separate from company borrowing costs and unquantified debt exposure.

findings.subject: Sector specificity and missing exposures
findings.finding: The reviewed model uses consumer-products demand and cost channels and introduces no insurance underwriting, reserve or portfolio assumptions. Missing debt, cash, working-capital, ownership and project details remain disclosed limitations.

assumptions.basis: Year-over-year reported sales growth applied to FY2025 Q4 sales. Base moderates latest Q3 growth of 7%, including four percentage points of FX support, against Q2 growth of 1% and prior-year Q4 growth of 2%. Bear assumes stalled growth; bull sustains latest momentum. These are aggregate assumptions; historical volume, pricing and FX contributions are not added again.

Gross profit as a fraction of sales. Base is close to prior-year Q4's 0.4911 and slightly below latest Q3's 0.4951, reflecting seasonal caution and recent compression from Q2's 0.5122. Bear assumes further compression; bull assumes partial recovery. Specific commodity, tariff or productivity causes are not established.

SG&A as a fraction of sales. Base anchors to prior-year Q4's 0.2826 and latest Q3's 0.2795. Bear assumes expense pressure and weaker sales absorption; bull assumes better absorption and spending efficiency. Higher ratios are adverse; no headcount or spending plan is inferred.

Quarterly signed interest expense plus interest income plus other income under the model contract. Base normalizes near prior-year Q4's 166 rather than carrying latest Q3's 414, which includes unusually high other income of 537. Q2's component total was 55. Bear allows a net expense; bull allows stronger contributions without fully repeating Q3. Classification conflicts and recurrence remain unresolved.

Tax expense as a fraction of pretax income. Base lies between prior-year Q4's 0.198 and latest Q3's 0.208, with Q2 at 0.201. Bear assumes a less favorable tax mix; bull assumes a favorable mix. These sensitivities do not assert specific tax events; higher tax rates are adverse.

Quarterly total net income attributable to noncontrolling interests, subtracted after tax. Base is near latest Q3's 19, with prior-year Q4 at 11 and Q1 at 31. Bear increases the deduction from parent earnings; bull reduces it. The scenario orientation concerns parent profitability, not a forecast of subsidiary performance.

Quarterly diluted weighted-average denominator. Historical NI/EPS approximations decline from about 2443 in prior-year Q4 to 2412 in latest Q3. Base assumes a modest further decline; bear allows a higher denominator and bull a larger decline. Lower shares favor EPS, not operating profit. No authorized repurchase volume or financing capacity is established.

Quarterly operating cash flow divided by total net income. Base gives substantial weight to prior-year Q4's seasonal 1.3748 but tempers it toward latest Q3's 1.0238. Bear assumes limited seasonal cash conversion improvement; bull assumes stronger conversion. Higher ratios favor cash generation without directly increasing accounting profit; working-capital detail is absent.

Positive capital expenditure outflow as a fraction of sales. Base is close to prior-year Q4's 0.0477 and latest Q3's 0.0480, allowing modest spending pressure. Bear assumes heavier cash investment; bull assumes lower cash intensity. Lower capex favors near-term free cash flow, without establishing superior long-term investment economics or directly changing modeled earnings.

Percent-to-decimal conversions and positive modeled capex outflows follow the contract. Cash conversion uses total net income rather than parent-attributable income.

findings.subject: Reconciliation and other-income classification
findings.finding: Original excerpts confirm the disclosed USD 1 million reconciliation differences and inconsistent operating/nonoperating labels. The conditional contract mapping is transparent, but neither exact historical reconciliation nor recurring classification of other income is established. These discrepancies were acknowledged without correction or certainty claims.

findings.subject: Research causality and double counting
findings.finding: Returning no research signals is justified by the empty evidence array. Historical FX, price and volume contributions describe reported growth without proving incremental causal effects. Scenario sales growth is aggregate, and the supplied assumptions do not add those contributions again or separately duplicate other income.

findings.subject: Scenario bounds and orientation
findings.finding: All nine drivers in all three scenarios fall within contractual bounds and use the required units. Adverse and favorable directions are consistent with parent earnings, EPS and near-term cash generation. Exact spreads remain explicitly judgmental sensitivities rather than sourced estimates or official guidance.

findings.subject: Precision and missing supporting detail
findings.finding: Four-decimal share approximations are computational precision, not observed denominator precision; the rounding limitation is disclosed. Cash seasonality, other-income recurrence and absent exposure or financing detail appropriately limit inference. No insurance-specific assumptions or unsupported insurance claims appear.

assumptions.basis: Reported YoY sales growth applied to same-quarter-prior-year sales. Retain the frozen control in all scenarios: base moderates Q3's 7% reported growth, including approximately four points of FX, against Q2's 1% and prior-year Q4's 2%. PG07/PG09 affordability and modest real spending offset possible pricing support and PG10 demand resilience; no calibrated net adjustment is justified. Use one joint demand assessment, without adding historical contributions again. Annual organic guidance of 0–4% does not constrain quarterly reported growth.

Gross profit divided by sales. Frozen control bear/base/bull of 0.475/0.490/0.505 already reflects historical compression and Q4 seasonality. Apply incremental reductions of 80/40/20 basis points respectively for the changed commodity outlook in PG06, corroborated by PG08 input and freight inflation. The base assumes some additional cost pressure reaches Q4; bear assumes greater recognition and weaker mitigation, while bull assumes procurement lag and offsets. These magnitudes are illustrative, not measured elasticities. Treat PG06/PG08 as one capped cost adjustment; do not repeat Q3 compression or allocate annual after-tax commodity, tariff, or FX amounts mechanically.

SG&A divided by sales; higher ratios are adverse. Retain all frozen scenarios, anchored near prior-year Q4's 0.2826 and latest Q3's 0.2795. Bear captures expense pressure and weaker absorption; bull captures improved efficiency and absorption. PG10 establishes peer performance but no P&G spending response, so an additional competitive expense charge would be unsupported and could duplicate existing downside.

Quarterly signed interest expense plus interest income plus other income under the contract. Retain the frozen scenarios: base normalizes near prior-year Q4's 166 rather than repeating Q3's 414, which contains other income of 537; Q2's component sum was 55. Bear permits net expense and bull stronger contributions. PG05 supplies policy-rate context but no debt repricing exposure, so no incremental interest adjustment is justified. Other-income recurrence and classification remain uncertain.

Tax expense divided by pretax income; higher rates are adverse. Retain all frozen scenarios. Base lies between prior-year Q4's 0.198 and latest Q3's 0.208, with Q2 at 0.201. Bear/bull reflect unfavorable/favorable tax-mix uncertainty without asserting specific tax events. Eligible market evidence supplies no supported incremental tax change.

Quarterly noncontrolling earnings deducted after tax from total net income. Retain the frozen scenarios: base is near latest Q3's 19, with prior-year Q4 at 11 and Q1 at 31. A larger deduction is adverse to parent earnings. No supplied market evidence supports changing these assumptions or establishes subsidiary profitability.

Quarterly diluted weighted-average EPS denominator. Retain the frozen scenarios, informed by approximate historical denominators declining from 2443 in prior-year Q4 to 2412 in latest Q3. Base assumes a modest further decline; bear/bull use higher/lower denominators, adverse/favorable to EPS. Historical estimates use attributable income divided by rounded EPS and are not reported share counts. No incremental repurchase or financing evidence supports a change.

Quarterly OCF divided by total net income. Retain the frozen scenarios: base weights prior-year Q4's seasonal 1.3748 while tempering toward latest Q3's 1.0238. Bear/bull reflect weaker/stronger cash conversion, affecting cash generation rather than accounting profitability. Input-cost evidence does not quantify working-capital effects, so no additional cash-conversion adjustment is made.

Positive capital expenditure outflow divided by sales. Retain all frozen scenarios, with base near prior-year Q4's 0.0477 and latest Q3's 0.0480. Bear assumes heavier cash investment; bull lower near-term cash intensity. Lower capex favors modeled free cash flow without directly improving earnings or establishing better long-term economics. No eligible investment-plan evidence supports an incremental change.

Cannot verify that supplied quotations, transcriptions, publication dates, hashes, or provenance match external webpages. Several material guidance and macro facts remain transcription-dependent.

The 2026-05-15 cutoff is an information-availability boundary; the October review timestamp does not itself introduce look-ahead.

findings.subject: Initial arithmetic blocker resolved within displayed precision
findings.finding: Supplemental original-source excerpts explicitly state that certain columns and rows may not add due to rounding. Independently recomputed residuals are USD 1 million: FY2025 Q3 sales-to-gross-profit +1, gross-profit-to-operating-income -1, and pretax bridge +1; FY2026 Q1 pretax bridge +1; FY2026 Q3 operating bridge +1, pretax bridge +1, and net-income bridge -1. These are consistent with rounding of multiple million-dollar inputs. Acceptance preserves every reported amount and residual; it does not establish exact underlying reconciliation. The curator's USD 2 million tolerance is not company guidance and is unnecessary to this conclusion.

findings.subject: Accounting labels versus model bridge
findings.finding: Original excerpts continue to label other income operating in FY2025 Q3 and FY2026 Q1–Q3, while FY2025 Q4 labels it non-operating. Supplemental evidence does not resolve that literal classification difference. The narrowly scoped mapping is nevertheless coherent as the explicitly defined bridge between displayed operating and pretax income, preserving original labels and disclosing the conflict. Pass does not certify that these amounts are accounting non-operating income.

findings.subject: Transcription-dependent support
findings.finding: Short quotations support selected facts but do not establish all annual guidance amounts and scopes, macro metric details, or peer category figures. Located factual extracts supply those missing details without an apparent quotation/transcription contradiction. Supplemental historical rounding quotations do not independently verify these market facts; source_accuracy remains not_verified.

findings.subject: Scenario arithmetic, units, and precision
findings.finding: Gross-margin changes correctly equal 80/40/20 bp: 0.475−0.008=0.467, 0.490−0.004=0.486, and 0.505−0.002=0.503. The other eight drivers match the frozen control, and all nine remain within contract bounds. Quarterly versus annual columns, percent-to-decimal conversions, signed interest, million-share denominators, total-net-income cash conversion, and positive capex outflows are coherent. Derived shares are expressly approximate and ratios are labeled rounded.

findings.subject: Causal interpretation and double counting
findings.finding: The combined PG06/PG08 margin allowance is explicitly illustrative, with unknown quarterly recognition and mitigation. It neither mechanically allocates annual after-tax guidance nor repeats Q3 compression. Demand signals are assessed jointly; CPI is not assigned as P&G pricing, peer growth is not assigned as P&G share loss, and policy rates are not applied to invented debt exposures. The base margin reduction is permissible as an assumption, not compelled or calibrated by the evidence. PG05's unsupported claim that PG01 contains an annual interest/tax headwind is identified and excluded.

findings.subject: Availability and sector specificity
findings.finding: Supplied publication dates precede the cutoff. PG06–PG10 and FY2026 Q3 history are eligible for the mid-market vintage and remain excluded from pre-quarter eligibility. No target-quarter outcomes are supplied. Insurance-specific mapping does not apply to this consumer-products packet, and no insurance exposure is invented.

assumptions.basis: Same-quarter-prior-year growth against Q2 2025 earned premiums. Historical growth slowed from approximately 6.6% in Q2 to 2.6% in Q4. Base assumes modest growth near the latest pace; bear assumes stagnation and bull a recovery toward the earlier pace. Higher growth is favorable within the contract's positive underlying underwriting margins; no pricing-volume decomposition is supported.

Same-quarter-prior-year growth against Q2 2025 written premiums. Historical growth slowed from approximately 3.9% in Q2 to 1.1% in Q4. Base assumes continued subdued growth, bear modest contraction and bull recovery toward Q2's pace. Written growth represents business momentum and does not directly enter the core pretax equation; earned growth is modeled separately because recognition can lag writing.

Q2 2025 was 84.7%, Q3 83.9% and Q4 82.2%. Base retains some improvement while avoiding automatic extrapolation of the strongest quarter into Q2. Bear assumes underwriting deterioration to 88%; bull broadly sustains Q4 performance. Lower ratios favor profitability. Catastrophes and reserve development remain separate drivers.

Positive quarterly losses, net of reinsurance. Q2 2025 losses were 927, versus its excerpted prior-year comparator of 1509; Q1 2025 losses were 2266 and Q4 only 95. Base stays near the same-quarter baseline rather than extrapolating Q4's unusually low amount. Bear assumes substantial losses below the supplied Q1 stress reference; bull assumes a lighter quarter with meaningful losses remaining. These are illustrative severities, not actuarial expected-loss estimates.

Positive favorable development increases pretax income. Q2 and Q4 releases were 315 and 321, but Q3 was only 22; Q1 was 378. Base discounts the larger recurring references for uncertainty, bear assumes minimal releases and bull approaches the strongest supplied quarterly observation. No reserve adequacy analysis establishes that releases will continue.

Quarterly pretax net investment income rose from 942 in Q2 to 1033 in Q3 and 1054 in Q4. Base assumes modest further growth from the latest quarter; bear falls toward Q2's level and bull extends the improvement more strongly. Higher income favors profitability. Portfolio balances, yields and alternative-investment contributions are unavailable, so these extensions have no supported causal decomposition.

Retains the signed expense convention and includes interest once. Q2 expense was 89 and Q4 expense 101, with the supplied quarters clustered around that range. Base approximates the latest expense; bear assumes a larger expense burden and bull a modest improvement. No separate debt or interest-rate projection is inferred.

Historical core tax expense divided by core pretax income was approximately 19.8% in Q2 and 19.6% in Q4. Base centers on those references. Bear assumes a higher effective burden and bull a lower burden as profitability sensitivities, without claiming supported changes in tax law or income mix. The orientation assumes positive pretax income; higher tax rates would not necessarily be adverse in a loss scenario.

Quarterly diluted weighted average shares declined from 229.3 in Q2 to 227.5 in Q3 and 224 in Q4. Base assumes modest continuation, bear holds at the latest level and bull assumes a larger further decline. Lower shares favor EPS when income is positive, without changing total income. This is a denominator sensitivity, not an observed or funded future buyback schedule.

findings.subject: Historical finance mappings and cutoff
findings.finding: Material Q2 baseline, Q4 latest-history and supporting-trend values agree with the original supplied excerpts. Supplied publication dates precede 2026-03-31. Quarterly values are distinguished from YTD/full-year values; premium growth uses same-quarter-prior-year denominators, ratios become decimals, and shares remain million diluted weighted average shares.

findings.subject: Insurance specificity and double counting
findings.finding: Mappings retain catastrophe losses net of reinsurance, convert them to positive losses for subtraction, add favorable development once, and retain interest within other income. Written premiums do not enter core pretax directly. Claims and expense components are reconciliation references rather than additional deductions. After-tax realized gains are distinguished from pretax investment income and core earnings.

findings.subject: Historical reconciliation
findings.finding: Independent arithmetic confirms Q2 and Q4 reported-minus-proxy underwriting residuals of -36.913 and -40.344 USD million. Reported underwriting plus investment and other income ties to reported core pretax; tax and after-tax realized gains reconcile the cited core and net income figures. The outputs appropriately avoid claiming an exact underwriting tie.

findings.subject: Research and scenario assumptions
findings.finding: The empty evidence array supports returning no incremental causal signals. All nine scenario drivers satisfy contract bounds and units. Assumptions are explicitly illustrative judgments anchored to supplied history, without unsupported actuarial, portfolio or buyback certainty. Under the supplied formula, pretax income remains positive across scenarios, supporting the stated tax and share-count profitability orientations.

findings.subject: Operating cash-flow period attribution
findings.finding: The excerpt contains the cited cash amounts but omits period headers. The assigned 2025 quarters sum to 10,606 USD million, which supports internal consistency but does not establish column attribution. Finance acknowledges this limitation; cash-period mapping receives no independent source attestation.

findings.subject: Scope of scenario coverage and precision
findings.finding: Passing these narrowly stated checks does not validate forecast accuracy, probabilities or final financial outputs. Contract limits exclude adverse reserve development and constrain underwriting stress. Historical ratios are rounded, target residuals and realized gains are unspecified, and precise scenario inputs should remain illustrative rather than presented as calibrated estimates.

assumptions.basis: Retain the frozen control for same-quarter-prior-year earned growth. Q2 historical growth was approximately 6.6%, slowing to 2.6% in Q4, supporting a modest 3% base. TRV01's 6.1% Business Insurance renewal premium change includes exposure and overlaps historical momentum; segment weights and earning lags do not support an incremental total-company adjustment. Bear stagnation and bull recovery remain illustrative profitability sensitivities.

Retain the frozen same-quarter-prior-year control: historical written growth slowed from approximately 3.9% in Q2 to 1.1% in Q4. TRV01 supports qualitative renewal persistence but provides no incremental total-company growth calibration. Bear contraction and bull recovery reflect business momentum; written premiums do not independently add to current core earnings.

Retain control base and bull against Q2/Q3/Q4 underlying ratios of 84.7%/83.9%/82.2%. Increase only the control bear from 88% to 89%, an illustrative additional one-percentage-point current-accident-year severity stress informed by TRV04's structural litigation-risk evidence. Its 2023 industry estimate is stale and does not establish current Travelers inflation. Lower ratios favor profitability. This incremental stress is not repeated in catastrophe losses or prior-year reserve development.

Retain all control values as positive quarterly pretax losses net of reinsurance. Q2 2025 losses of 927 and its prior-year comparator of 1509 support seasonal context; Q1 losses of 2266 and Q4 losses of 95 demonstrate volatility. TRV05 supplies prospective drought uncertainty but no Travelers exposure or insured-loss mapping. The existing wide stress range is retained without an unsupported incremental dollar adjustment. Higher losses are adverse.

Retain the frozen control. Q2 and Q4 favorable releases of 315 and 321 support the discounted base, while Q3's 22 demonstrates variability and Q1's 378 anchors the favorable case. Higher positive releases benefit profitability. TRV04 does not establish Travelers reserve strengthening; its incremental stress is assigned solely to underlying underwriting, avoiding duplication. These assumptions do not establish reserve adequacy.

Retain quarterly pretax control values against income of 942 in Q2, 1033 in Q3 and 1054 in Q4. The base already assumes modest further growth. TRV02 repeats the Q4 observation and attributes historical growth to assets and long-term yield; it does not justify stacking another uplift. TRV03's maintained policy range supports zero immediate policy-change adjustment. Portfolio and reinvestment data cannot calibrate additional dollar sensitivities. Higher income is favorable.

Retain the frozen signed-expense control, anchored by Q2 expense of 89 and Q4 expense of 101. Bear assumes a greater expense burden and bull modest improvement. No incremental evidence supports a change or a separate debt-cost forecast; interest remains included once.

Retain the control, supported by historical core tax-to-pretax rates of approximately 19.8% in Q2 and 19.6% in Q4. Bear and bull are higher/lower effective-burden sensitivities, without an asserted tax-law or income-mix change. Higher rates are adverse under the positive-pretax-income orientation; the relationship can reverse with losses.

Retain the control against quarterly diluted weighted-average shares of 229.3 in Q2, 227.5 in Q3 and 224 in Q4. Base assumes modest continuation of the decline, bear holds the latest level, and bull assumes a larger decline. No incremental market evidence supports revision. Lower shares favor EPS with positive income; this is a denominator assumption, not a verified or funded buyback schedule.

assumptions.basis: Same-quarter-prior-year growth, applied to Q2 2025 earned premiums of 10,921. Base rounds the latest Q1 decline of approximately 0.98%, giving recent weakness more weight than Q4's positive growth. Bear assumes deeper contraction; bull assumes modest recovery. Same-quarter-prior-year growth, applied to Q2 2025 written premiums of 11,543. Base approximates latest Q1's 1.68% decline after roughly 1% growth in Q4. Base carries most of latest Q1's 85.3% ratio into Q2, versus the prior-year Q2 seasonal reference of 84.7%; it avoids extrapolating Q4's stronger 82.2%. Bear stresses underlying loss and expense pressure; bull assumes improved underwriting efficiency. Higher ratios reduce profitability. Catastrophes and reserve development remain separate.

Positive pretax losses net of reinsurance. Base is slightly above Q2 2025's 927, recognizing the same source's Q2 2024 comparison of 1,509 rather than carrying forward Q4's unusually low 95. Bear exceeds both Q2 references but remains below the supplied Q1 2025 loss of 2,266; bull represents a lighter-loss quarter. These are severity judgments, not distribution-derived expectations.

Positive favorable releases add to profit. Base modestly discounts prior-year Q2's 315 and does not mechanically repeat latest Q1's 413. Bear assumes no releases; bull assumes releases slightly above latest Q1. Q3 2025's 22 demonstrates variability. The contract prevents modeling negative development.

Quarterly pretax net investment income. Base lies between latest Q1's 1,008 and Q4's 1,054, above prior-year Q2's 942, without assuming uninterrupted sequential growth. Bear assumes weaker investment earnings; bull assumes stronger earnings. Portfolio yield, balances and alternative-investment contributions are not separately forecast.

Signed quarterly pretax income/expense including interest. Base stays near latest Q1's -111, versus Q4's -101 and prior-year Q2's -89. Bear assumes additional expense pressure; bull returns toward the historical expense range. Interest is already included and must not be deducted again.

Core effective tax rate. Base is near prior-year Q2's 371/1,875 and Q4's 612/3,123, rather than assuming latest Q1's lower 374/2,070 persists. Bear and bull impose higher and lower tax burdens for profitability sensitivity. This orientation is deliberate; actual tax rates may move differently with earnings mix and tax preferences.

Quarterly weighted-average diluted shares. Base assumes a further moderate decline from latest Q1's 218.4 after Q4's 224.0. Bear assumes repurchases pause and modest dilution; bull assumes a larger further reduction. These are denominator sensitivities without a funding forecast. Lower shares benefit positive core EPS but do not increase core income.

assumptions.basis: Retain all control scenarios. Same-quarter-prior-year growth uses Q2 2025 earned premiums of 10,921 as its baseline. Retain control base and bull; increase bear from 0.88 to 0.89, an incremental 1 percentage-point joint current-period severity stress. Retain all control scenarios as positive quarterly pretax losses net of reinsurance. Base is modestly above Q2 2025's 927; its reported Q2 2024 comparison of 1,509 supports substantial seasonal uncertainty. Bear represents heavier losses and bull lighter losses. Retain all control scenarios. Positive favorable releases increase profit. Base discounts prior-year Q2's 315 rather than repeating latest Q1's 413; Q3's 22 illustrates variability.
